ranked.headline: Frameworks decode cell states, spatial niches, and perturbation effects from omics data
ranked.summary: Spatial CRISPR screening and niche-level communication inference are now being built on explicit statistical models.

ranked.headline: Computational frameworks defining what single-cell and genomic experiments can resolve
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications formalize power, bias correction, and mediation inference for Perturb-seq and single-cell multi-omic experiments.

ranked.headline: Biomedical prediction models tested for shortcut, memorization and missingness failures
ranked.summary: Recent work tests biomedical predictors on external validation, missing data blocks, and shortcut risks rather than accuracy alone.

ranked.headline: Computational ranking of variants and sgRNAs for pathogenicity and HDR correction
ranked.summary: Foundation-model and proteome-scale scores now prioritize variants, while cohort prevalence is being added to guide selection for TP53 correction.

ranked.headline: Interpretable ML infers disease drivers and mechanisms from patient omics profiles
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair interpretable model structure with mechanistic and endpoint-specific outputs across single-cell, multi-omics, and clinical data.

ranked.headline: Microbial sequence models pair cross-modal alignment with domain-restricted pretraining
ranked.summary: Preprints from May 2026 pair protein and genomic language model embeddings with alignment, distillation, and retrieval objectives.

ranked.headline: Structure models predict cryptic pockets, antimicrobial targets and ADMET liabilities
ranked.summary: Structure-grounded machine learning and dynamics workflows now extend design predictions to cryptic pockets, targets and ADMET liabilities.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models predict variant effects and gene expression from genomic sequence
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend sequence-to-expression and vision-based genomic models to variant pathogenicity, splicing, and tumor interpretation.

ranked.headline: Network and atlas tools link metabolic, lipid, and glycan data across omics layers
ranked.summary: Preprints now pair public metabolome atlases and lipidomics environments with directed network models of metabolic flow and formal rewiring tests.

ranked.headline: Pretrained biomolecular models are being reused across protein and RNA design tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair pretrained protein and RNA foundation models with generative search for sequence and structure design.

ranked.headline: Long-read workflows and haplotype-resolved pangenomes recover complex genomic regions
ranked.summary: Long-read sequencing now resolves near-complete haplotypes and microbial genomes, making end-to-end workflow choices decisive for recovery.

ranked.headline: Standardized benchmarks now make omics inference method performance an explicit result
ranked.summary: Spatial cell-cell communication and TAD calling methods are now benchmarked directly, with performance reported alongside inference outputs.

ranked.headline: Computational methods align single-cell and spatial data and process 3D microscopy stacks
ranked.summary: Atlas-scale single-cell and spatial datasets and terabyte-scale 3D imaging are driving scalable, interpretable computational pipelines.

ranked.headline: Learned models and simulation target protein flexibility, disorder and binding paths
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair protein language models, network analysis and MD with flexibility and disorder as shared modelling targets.

ranked.headline: Computational design tools address codon, splicing, primer and assembly bottlenecks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications describe open computational methods for mRNA codon design, missplicing, RT-qPCR primer ranking and oligopool gene assembly.

ranked.headline: Sequence models infer influenza host source, JEV mutations, and vaccine protection
ranked.summary: Sequence-based ML and Bayesian models now link viral genotype to host source, spillover risk, T cell escape, and vaccine protection.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale and long-read assemblies of wheat, a shrub, and sugarcane
ranked.summary: Long-read and Hi-C assemblies now resolve phased polyploid and non-model plant genomes, enabling trait-linked analysis in crop species.

ranked.headline: Random networks and digital twins test mechanisms against neural population data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints score explicit network models against population recordings and latent representations, moving beyond prediction accuracy alone.

ranked.headline: Reference-free and classifier-based tools resolve microbial and viral sequence data
ranked.summary: Proteome-scale, reference-free and tree-classifier workflows now address phylogenetic and taxonomic inference across prokaryotes and viruses.

ranked.headline: Open tools resolve strains, duplications and species from microbiome sequencing data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method extend metagenomic and amplicon analysis to strain, mechanism and species resolution.

ranked.headline: Biological language models applied to peptide activity and viral genomics benchmarks
ranked.summary: Biological language models and graph transformers are now being benchmarked and applied to peptide toxicity, antimicrobial, and viral sequence prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Metabolic inference moves toward model uncertainty and multi-dataset flux estimation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications address model uncertainty, multi-dataset flux estimation, and enzyme constraints in metabolic inference.

ranked.headline: Learned models steer biomolecular structure, design and ligand binding prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair pretrained diffusion, flow and graph models with structural proteomics, dynamics and benchmark-bias corrections.

ranked.headline: Ontology-aligned knowledge graphs make literature and metabolomics data computable
ranked.summary: Literature-derived and molecular knowledge graphs now carry explicit provenance and directed-propagation semantics for inference.

ranked.headline: Nuclear morphology is being linked to single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles
ranked.summary: Million-nucleus datasets now allow nuclear morphology to be tied to transcriptomic states in mouse embryo, mouse heart, and human cortex.

ranked.headline: Sequence and structure comparison methods across viral genomes, RNA, proteins, k-mers
ranked.summary: Four May 2026 preprints modify encoding or search procedures to improve alignment and comparison of biological sequences, structures, and k-mer indices.

ranked.headline: Integrating multiple predictors to resolve transcript structure and isoform features
ranked.summary: Recent tools combine Ribo-seq, long- and short-read RNA-seq, and multi-predictor polyA calls to refine isoform annotation.

ranked.headline: Inferring mosaic chromosome Y loss and somatic CNA states from sequencing data
ranked.summary: Bulk RNA-seq, single-cell CNA and plasma miRNA profiles are now tested as proxies against independent DNA-based or reference measurements.

ranked.headline: Reference genome and library prep choices shape genomic analysis accuracy
ranked.summary: Truth-set and multi-assay benchmarks now quantify how reference and workflow choices alter downstream genomic results.

ranked.headline: Shifted conformational ensembles explain how single substitutions alter protein function
ranked.summary: Recent MD studies of IP3R1, pyruvate kinase, and PARP1 link single-residue changes and inhibitor contacts to shifted ensembles or communication networks.

ranked.headline: Environmental and polymer constraints shape viral and microbial genome organization
ranked.summary: Recent items separate null-model and host-associated constraints from specific interactions in bacterial chromosomes and viral genomes.

ranked.headline: Predicted phosphosite functions, tumor progression paths, and LECA interactome
ranked.summary: Recent items apply computational inference to phosphosite function, tumor progression order, and ancestral protein networks.

ranked.headline: Computational prioritization of drugs, degraders, and microbial metabolites
ranked.summary: Computational tools now link gene sets, structural proteomics, and mass spectrometry to prioritized drugs, degraders, and bioactive metabolites.

ranked.headline: New software formats and libraries speed up genomic and phylogenetic computation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a publication describe performance-oriented software rewrites for sequence data formats and phylogenetic computation at scale.

ranked.headline: Network topology and heterogeneity shape fixation, prevalence, and epidemic outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published model quantify how network structure and behavioral heterogeneity alter fixation and spread outcomes.

ranked.headline: Cryo-EM methods resolve flexible and continuous conformational states of proteins
ranked.summary: Cryo-EM and cryo-ET pipelines now model flexible domains and continuous conformational landscapes at atomic or in situ resolution.

ranked.headline: Timescale and quasi-steady-state assumptions reshape biological transition geometry
ranked.summary: Timescale coordinates and quasi-steady-state validity now bear directly on metastability and tipping-point timing in biological models.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics links structural variation and selection to trait evolution
ranked.summary: Large genome collections now enable population-scale tests of structural variant history, chromosome evolution, and convergent adaptation across lineages.

ranked.headline: Graph and causal network models are resolving tissue-specific genetic risk architecture
ranked.summary: Recent GWAS-based methods now encode tissue context, LD structure, and causal feedback directly in network models of complex disease risk.

ranked.headline: Cell-type, population and subcellular resolution link transcription to function
ranked.summary: Preprints now pair cell-type, population and subcellular profiling to tie gene expression to symbiosis, fungal ecology and heterocyst biology.
